intro: Degrees of friendship, love affairs, and the ceremonies where everyone meets.
p.ligar: to chat up, to pick up
p.asistir a.nota: False friend: it does not mean to assist.
p.caer bien.nota: Me cae bien: I like him.
b1.titulo: How well do you know them?
b1.texto:
**Degrees.** **Lo conozco de vista** (I have seen him around). **Es un conocido.** **Es un compañero.** **Es un amigo.** **Es un amigo íntimo.** **Es un amigo de toda la vida.** **Es como de la familia.**

**Liking people.** Not gustar, which suggests attraction, but **caer**: **me cae bien**, **me cae fatal**, **me cayó genial**.

**Getting on.** **Llevarse bien con**, **tratar con**, **relacionarse con**, **hacer amigos**, **mantener una relación**, **tener confianza con** alguien.

**Love.** **Ligar** (to chat someone up), **un ligue**, **salir con** alguien, **estar prometido**, **tener un compromiso**, **romper con** alguien, **tener un lío** (an affair, colloquial).

**Occasions.** **Un nacimiento**, **un bautizo**, **una primera comunión**, **una boda**, **un aniversario**. Twenty-five years of marriage are **las bodas de plata**, and fifty are **las bodas de oro**. **El santo** is the day of the saint you are named after.

**What happens there.** **El anfitrión** receives **los invitados**. There is **una ceremonia** and then **un banquete**. Someone **da un discurso** or **dice unas palabras**, everybody **brinda**, and the presents are **envueltos** and then **desenvueltos**.

**Verbs for events.** **Celebrar**, **organizar**, **cancelar**, **asistir a**. Careful: **asistir a una boda** is to attend it. To help is **ayudar**.
b2.f0: Last Saturday I attended the silver wedding of Blanca and Rodrigo, lifelong friends.
b2.f1: They met at a christening, hit it off that same afternoon and, against all the odds, have never broken up.
b2.f2: There were almost a hundred guests, of whom I knew ten well and another twenty by sight.
b2.f3: After a simple ceremony there was a banquet that lasted until night.
b2.f4: The eldest son gave such a funny speech that even his grandmother, who never laughs, ended up crying with laughter.
b2.f5: We drank a toast to the hosts and to their having another twenty-five years together.
b2.f6: They sat me next to a cousin of Rodrigo's whom I couldn't stand at first and with whom I ended up dancing.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, where did Blanca and Rodrigo meet?
b4.o2.refuerzo: The banquet is at their anniversary.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what did the writer think of Rodrigo's cousin at first?
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I like your brother (as a person).
b7.o0.refuerzo: Caer bien: to be liked as a person.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Me gusta tu hermano suggests attraction.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Llevarse bien needs me llevo bien con él.
b9.o0: I only know him by sight.
b9.o1.explicacion: Conocer de vista: to know by sight.
b9.o2: I only see him when I know him.
b9.o2.explicacion: Conocer de vista: to know by sight.
b10.traduccion: We drank a toast to the hosts of the party.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the account of a wedding or another celebration you attended, with details of the guests and the ceremony.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud the difference between an acquaintance, a friend and a close friend, with examples from your life.
